result:
**Verdict: NO-GO.** One blocker remains, and it is a wording fix. The B1 fix created it: the delta promises that legacy v2 builds keep byte-identical reports after migration, and the main v2 report schema makes that impossible. B2 and M1–M5 are resolved.

## Remaining blocker

**N1 (blocker): the legacy v2 compatibility claim is wrong because the report hashes the dependency file.**
- **Where:**
  - CN-166-P1, "Compatibility, migration and affected consumers", second bullet (line 124): "With the class added, their legacy manifest/report bytes stay unchanged."
  - CN-166-P1, "Changed acceptance": "Freeze existing legacy tests/goldens unchanged."
  - Design §7, line 244: "unchanged legacy output after migration", and line 265: "legacy goldens remain unchanged".
  - `provenance-core-inbox.md` line 31: "old legacy goldens remain byte-identical under approved migration".
- **What the schema says:** main `build-report-v2.schema.json` lists `dependenciesHash` as a required field (lines 16 and 58–60). The new `graphicContentClass` is required on every v2 resolution of a `GraphicRevisionSource`, so migration has to add it to the dependency input. The manifest has no dependency hash, so the manifest claim can hold. The report claim can't.
- **Failure example:**
  1. An accepted v2 fixture has an `OccurrenceMediaResolutionV2` with `sourceSnapshot.system:"graphic_asset"` for a `graphic_revision` source.
  2. After the change, the frozen dependency input fails with `GRAPHIC_PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE`, because "old unclassified dependency inputs fail until migrated".
  3. After migration it compiles. Assuming `dependenciesHash` covers the dependency input (as its name says), the report gets a new `dependenciesHash` value, so its golden no longer matches byte for byte.
  4. An implementer of #218 now has to make an unapproved choice:
     - exclude the new field from `dependenciesHash`, which changes what that hash means; or
     - update frozen fixtures and goldens, which breaks "freeze existing legacy tests/goldens unchanged".
- **Smallest fix:** replace the claim with the true effect, in CN-166-P1 and in the matching design and inbox lines:
  - v2 manifest bytes stay unchanged.
  - v2 report bytes stay unchanged except `dependenciesHash`, plus any field derived from it.
  - Existing frozen v2 fixtures and goldens that contain graphic-source resolutions get migrated copies, listed on the implementation baseline and covered by the explicit CN-166-P1 approval.
  - Everything else stays frozen.

  If the author would rather leave `dependenciesHash` material unchanged, that is a new decision and has to be stated outright. It can't be left implicit.

## Prior findings

| Finding | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Resolved (but the fix caused N1) | `graphicContentClass` is required on every `GraphicRevisionSource` resolution, has no default and is forbidden on other resolutions. `manual`/`derived` need a matching content record of the same kind; `legacy_unclassified` must have no content record and no binding; `derived` requires the binding. A missing class or content record produces `GRAPHIC_PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE`. Only storage positively identified as the pre-provenance format may produce `legacy_unclassified`. A deliberately false classification from the trusted resolver is named as an upstream integrity failure. In my example, a dropped content record can no longer compile as legacy. The v1 writer-omission residual is stated, assigned to #64/#9, routed to the Producer (design §8.1) and tested ("v1 writer omission"). |
| B2 | Resolved | `projectRevisionId` now uses the accepted #7 pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (script-document-v1 line 373, compiler-dependencies-v1 line 93). `projectId` stays the UUID `EntityId`, the same as accepted #7 `resolvedGraphics.projectId` (compiler-dependencies-v1 line 92). |
| M1 | Resolved | `GRAPHIC_PROVENANCE_UNEXPECTED` covers duplicate or unused snapshot and content records. Manual bindings forbid a snapshot pointer. |
| M2 | Resolved | `contentHash` is SHA-256 over the exact retained bytes. The synthetic example is now labelled as a canonical-serialized extract. |
| M3 | Resolved, and the correction stands | Main `DiagnosticCodeV2` (lines 393–420) is a closed enum, so v2 does need the enum additions. v1 relies on the existing open code pattern. My earlier generalization to v2 was wrong. |
| M4 | Resolved | #218 is recorded with its retained Inbox body. It says it is unclaimed and undispatched, sits behind #166/#7/#20, and requires CN-166-P1 approval first. |
| M5 | Resolved | `VERIFICATION_POLICY.md` line 84 now refers to the every-ticket rule. The waiver and heartbeat rules (lines 92–116) and the "Qualified cloud substitution" section (line 135) are intact. |

## Optional suggestion (not a blocker)

- **S1: say what happens to new non-EV24 v2 graphics.** `ResolvedGraphicContent` only supports the EV24 semantic and template shape. If a new-format v2 graphic revision that isn't EV24 exists, the resolver can't emit `manual`/`derived` for it, and it can't emit `legacy_unclassified` because it isn't pre-provenance storage. So it would block. One sentence would settle it: such revisions stay in the pre-provenance storage format, resolving as `legacy_unclassified` (no derived-evidence claim), until their own contract is approved.

## Limitations

- I reviewed only this packet, with Read/Grep/Glob, no execution and no network.
- I haven't seen `compiler-core-v2.ts`, so I'm inferring from the field name that `dependenciesHash` covers the full dependency input. If it actually leaves out resolution fields, N1 shrinks to stating that explicitly.
- I can't list which accepted v2 fixtures contain graphic-source resolutions.
- I confirmed the #218 creation and its Inbox state only from the retained text.
- Scope check: no runtime, schema, generated, fixture or golden files are in the delta. The changes are limited to docs and policy.
